In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1).$

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1))^{′}}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡(2x-1)} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1)}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡(2x-1)}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1))^{′}}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡(2x-1)} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1)}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1))^{′}}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡(2x-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the derivative formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}},
$$

and the chain rule, we have

$$
(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1))^{′}=\frac{1}{1-(2x-1)^{2}}\cdot (2x-1)^{′}=\frac{2}{4x-4{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1)}-\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{(4x-4{x}^{2})\,{arcoth}^{2}⁡(2x-1)} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(2x-1)}-\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{4x-4{x}^{2}}\,\frac{1}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡(2x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$
